title: Q4 Strategy Reset + Culture Deep Dive
summary: Leadership presented a focused Q4 plan: tighten runway, prioritize high-impact product bets (Serving runtime and Redwood Optimize), pause non-critical hiring, and double down on reliability SLAs. People team explained changes to performance review cadence and support resources. Open Q&A surfaced concerns about promotions, dedicated customers, and deferred features. Several follow-ups were assigned.
next_steps: Maya to circulate a simplified 90-day plan and revised OKRs by 2026-11-24
Samir to publish a short MOP (maintenance & operations plan) for infra reliability targets by 2026-11-30
Lina to share trimmed product roadmap with canary rollouts and de-prioritized items by 2026-11-25
People (Priya) to host two listening sessions for ICs on 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-23

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes
Venue: All-hands video call (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Lina Gomez, Derek Shaw, Priya Kapoor + company-wide
Shared artifacts: Q4-priorities-deck.pdf (link), trimmed-roadmap.xlsx (link), MOP-draft.md (link - coming)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on such short notice. I know it's late for some of you, appreciate it. We'll run through why we're resetting priorities for Q4 and then open for questions — short and honest.

[00:18] Maya Chen: Quick note, transcription may be rough, apologies if names get munged. Okay, slide one, runway and market context, um, in short, macro headwinds continue and we've got a responsibility to extend runway while still investing in the things that deliver product-market fit.

[00:34] Samir Patel: I'll do a very high level infra snapshot — we've seen median 95th percentile latency drift for a subset of models, that plus rising GPU spot prices means we need to optimize both software (KV cache, smart batching) and right-size some capacity. We're not talking about layoffs today, it's re-prioritization.

[00:52] Lina Gomez: From a product POV, we pulled data across Hosted API routes and Dedicated customers. Two big themes: customers care about predictable latency and observability. So we propose focusing on: 1) Serving runtime improvements for tail latency, 2) Redwood Optimize features to cut unit cost, and 3) finishing the routing/fallback work. Other non-core UX projects get delayed.

[01:15] Derek Shaw: Engineering will freeze non-critical feature branches and we will move engineers toward reliability and Optimize work. We have a list of non-blocking experiments that will be parked.

[01:32] Priya Kapoor: People update — we're changing the annual review cadence to a quarterly check-in for 90 days to make compensation and promotion discussions more continuous while we navigate this period. We'll also increase manager 1:1 coaching office hours.

[01:55] Maya Chen: I'll say explicitly: our mission hasn't changed, but how we allocate effort is tightening. We're prioritizing throughput to customers and cost-per-token wins because that buys more time and keeps customers happy.

[02:14] Audience (All Hands): A couple of text questions popped in. First, will the Dedicated customers see changes to their SLAs or pricing?

[02:29] Samir Patel: No SLA changes planned; if anything, Dedicated gets more focus for reliability. We're also looking at configuration defaults — some Dedicated pools are overprovisioned. We'll propose a plan to customers, communication will be coordinated by sales.

[02:48] Audience: Any hiring freeze?

[02:53] Maya Chen: We're pausing open reqs that are not mission-critical. Critical hires — the small list Derek will publish — will continue. Startups should always be careful with headcount; this is a surgical pause, not a blanket freeze.

[03:12] Audience: What does this mean for people on performance improvement plans (PIPs)?

[03:20] Priya Kapoor: We will continue to support folks; PIPs remain in place. Our emphasis is coaching and clarity. If anything, we're making expectations more frequent so people have more signal sooner.

[03:34] Lina Gomez: Let me show the trimmed roadmap — bear with the deck, I know it's denser than usual. (link posted) The big change: de-prioritize two low-adoption integrations, delay the experimental developer portal, and accelerate the bert-like quantization pass for serving. 'Bert-like' got munged in the slide note, sorry.

[04:02] Samir Patel: Quick technical thing — we're rolling a KV cache improvement that reduces warm-start tokens by about 20% in internal tests. Some folks might see it as small, but at scale that halves cost in some routes. Also new batching heuristics to reduce small-batch penalties, this helps low QPS tenants.

[04:28] Audience: Will this impact the roadmap for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers?

[04:35] Lina Gomez: Private stays supported; for on-prem customers with active contracts we'll prioritize critical fixes. New big feature work for Private may be pushed out unless tied to a committed deal.

[04:52] Maya Chen: We also need to talk about communication — going forward we'll share a simplified weekly note so everyone knows the top three priorities.

[05:03] Audience: People ops question — how will promotions be affected?

[05:10] Priya Kapoor: Promotions will still happen; timeline may be adjusted. The goal is to avoid surprises — more frequent check-ins give clearer ramps for promotions or role changes.

[05:27] Audience: Culture — this feels like a pivot, how should managers talk to their teams?

[05:35] Maya Chen: Be transparent, set clear priorities, and emphasize the why. We will give managers talking points and an FAQ. Priya and I will co-host manager sync tomorrow to walk through the script.

[05:58] (light cross talk, someone laughs)

[06:10] Samir Patel: Quick ops ask — if you see latency regressions, file an incident with the tag 'q4-priority' so we can triage faster and route to the right oncall.

[06:27] Audience (various): A few folks asked about stock/options and long-term incentives — will there be a refresh?

[06:36] Maya Chen: Compensation refreshes are evaluated case by case; we will not be doing a company-wide refresh in the next quarter. But leadership is committed to long-term programs — more on that when it's concrete.

[06:52] Derek Shaw: On the engineering front, a couple of concrete items: we'll roll a hotfix window next week that includes the KV cache change and a fallback routing improvement. We'll limit deploy traffic to canary regions first.

[07:10] Audience: Can we get a sense of the financial targets or runway extension?

[07:16] Maya Chen: High level: our aim is to extend runway by 6-9 months through cost savings and slowed hiring while still keeping critical product bets funded. I'll share numbers in the follow-up note.

[07:36] (someone types in chat: 'thanks for the clarity')

[07:45] Scene: quick applause emoji flood

[07:50] Maya Chen: Ok let's open for live questions — we'll do 20 minutes and then we need to end.

[08:05] Q&A segment (selected):
[08:10] Speaker - Gabe (Eng): Hey, will the Optimize changes require model changes or is it runtime only?

[08:18] Samir Patel: Mostly runtime and config changes; there are a couple of small model conversion steps for quantization but we have a plan to make that low-friction.

[08:30] Speaker - Nadia (Sales): For Dedicated customers, how do we frame the messaging around performance improvements without spooking them about reliability?

[08:38] Lina Gomez: Frame it as 'improving predictability and cost efficiency' — we will coordinate with account execs to share the MOP and roadmap items that affect them.

[08:50] Speaker - Marco (Customer Success): Will we offer migration help for Dedicated customers who want to downsize pools?

[08:58] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll create a playbook and a migration-support offer; Derek's team will be on the hook for a small set of migrations.

[09:10] Audience: Any external hiring changes? Are recruiters still sourcing?

[09:18] Priya Kapoor: Recruiters will continue to build candidate pipelines for future hires, but active offers will be limited to approved reqs.

[09:30] (small pause)

[09:40] Maya Chen: Before we close — some leadership reflections. This is a hard but normal part of company maturity. It doesn't mean we stop being ambitious; it means we pick where ambition must focus.

[09:56] Audience (All Hands): Thank you for the transparency.

[10:03] Maya Chen: Final housekeeping: we'll post full notes and the recorded session. Please RSVP for the manager sync tomorrow. Thanks, everyone.

[10:15] End of meeting notes.

Notes on transcription quality: automatic capture, medium accuracy; proper nouns sometimes mistaken (e.g., 'KV cache' as "K V cash", product names occasionally split). Some timestamps approximate.

Explicit recap (verbatim):
- Tighten priorities: focus on Serving runtime, Redwood Optimize, and routing/fallback work.
- Pause or delay non-critical UX and integrations.
- Surgical hiring pause; publish list of critical hires.
- Change review cadence to shorter check-ins + more manager support.

Meeting closed at ~17:12 UTC.
